guide.title: Model concepts
guide.subtitle: What each element of the model means and how the analysis uses it, with an example for each.
guide.open: Open this entry in the Guide

entity.title: Entity
entity.body: A domain object with a lifecycle: an aggregate, an entity or a value object. Entities are grouped by bounded context, which becomes a box in the map.
entity.example: Order, Payment and Shipment are three entities; Order lives in the Sales context, Payment in Payments.

states.title: States, initial and final
states.body: The states the entity can be in. The initial one is where it starts when it has no creation actions; final states end the lifecycle: they have no outgoing actions and an effect with “skip if already final” leaves them alone.

liveness.title: State liveness: active, off, deleted
liveness.body: For each state you say whether the entity operates (active), exists but is disabled and can be turned back on (off), or is gone with no way back (deleted). DOES_NOT_EXIST counts as deleted. Compositions rely on this.
liveness.example: Customer SUSPENDED is off (it can be reactivated); Customer REMOVED is deleted.

creation.title: Creation actions
creation.body: An entity can come into existence in several ways, each with its own checks: a creation action starts from DOES_NOT_EXIST and leads to a birth state. Without creation actions the entity starts from its initial state.
creation.example: Order: “Order from website” or “Order from marketplace”, with different guards.

actions.title: Actions (transitions)
actions.body: They move the entity from one state to another. They can have an actor, guards (conditions on other entities) and cascading effects (what happens to other entities).
actions.example: Order “ship” PAID → SHIPPING, run by the Warehouse.

cascade.title: Cascade only
cascade.body: An action the user does not run directly: it only happens as the effect of another one. The analysis reports the ones nothing triggers.
cascade.example: Invoice “issue credit note” only happens when the Order return is recorded.

guards.title: Guards
guards.body: Conditions on the states of other entities that must hold for the action to run. During a cascade they see the states already updated by the previous actions. Text rules are reminders to check by hand.
guards.example: “record payment” requires the Payment to be CAPTURED.

guardsOr.title: OR guards
guardsOr.body: Guards normally all apply together (AND). Linking them with OR, one of the group is enough.
guardsOr.example: “ship” requires the Payment CAPTURED or a Customer with approved credit.

guardsEach.title: “For each” guards
guardsEach.body: On a child entity of a composition, the guard can apply to every existing parent: each parent must have at least one child in the given states (with “must not be in”: none).
guardsEach.example: Confirming the Cart requires, for each Order, at least one AVAILABLE Order line.

effects.title: Cascading effects
effects.body: What an action does to other entities: move them to a state, make them run an action by name, or create them. Each effect must find on the child a transition that exists and whose guards pass: if it does not, the cascade is blocked.
effects.example: Order “cancel” → Payment to CANCELLED (the Payment needs a transition to CANCELLED).

skipFinal.title: Skip if already final
skipFinal.body: On an effect: if the entity involved is already in a final state it is left as is instead of reporting a conflict. Useful when the effect touches every instance and some are already concluded.
skipFinal.example: Cancelling the order cancels its lines, except the ones already SHIPPED.

composition.title: Composition
composition.body: A relation where the child cannot exist without the parent: when the parent is deleted the child must go, when it is turned off the child cannot stay active. Invariants and automatic checks follow from it.
composition.example: Order line is composed in Order: once the order is deleted, its lines must be deleted.

instances.title: Multiple instances
instances.body: On a composition you can ask the analysis to simulate 2-3 children per parent (#1, #2), to find cases like “one child confirmed and the other deleted”. Each parent copy has its own child copies. The simulator stays at one instance.
instances.example: Order with 2 Lines: the analysis also explores Line #1 SHIPPED with Line #2 CANCELLED.

invariants.title: Invariants
invariants.body: Combinations of states that must never exist together. The analysis looks for a path that gets there and, if it finds one, shows the shortest.
invariants.example: Forbidden: Order CANCELLED with Shipment SHIPPED.

analysis.title: Edge case analysis
analysis.body: It explores every combination of states reachable from the initial state and reports violable invariants, blocked cascades, missing transitions, deadlocks, never reached states and never executable actions. The “by cause” view groups the symptoms of the same cause.
analysis.example: 12 findings from 4 causes: fixing one cause removes all its symptoms.

missing.title: Missing transitions
missing.body: A cascading effect asks an entity to move from one state to another, but that transition does not exist. Add it (usually “cascade only”), or review the effect.
missing.example: Cancelling the order asks the Payment for FAILED → CANCELLED, which does not exist.

conflicts.title: Blocked cascades
conflicts.body: An action cannot complete its effects: a transition is missing, a guard blocks, the effects trigger each other forever, or it is unclear which action to pick. Each case suggests where to step in.
conflicts.example: Order “record return” is blocked because the credit note requires the Invoice ISSUED and finds it CANCELLED.

deadlock.title: Deadlock
deadlock.body: A combination where no action can run and some entity is not concluded. It is often a consequence of other causes: replay the path in the simulator to see which guard stops the actions.
deadlock.example: Shipment LOST with no outgoing action.

fix.title: Fix and preview
fix.body: For many findings the system proposes fixes you can apply with one click. “Preview” runs the analysis on the changed model without touching it and tells how many errors it solves or introduces.
fix.example: “Add to Payment the transition from FAILED to CANCELLED”: solves 2 errors.

ack.title: Accept or postpone
ack.body: If a finding is intended, accept it with a note; if you will think about it later, postpone it. It leaves the counts until the part of the model involved changes: then it comes back as “needs review”.
ack.example: “Refunds without invoice are handled by the back office”: accepted.

expectations.title: Expectations
expectations.body: Acceptance tests of the domain: goals that must stay reachable and paths (saved from the simulator) that must work or stay blocked. They are checked at every analysis.
expectations.example: Goal: it must be possible to reach Order DELIVERED with Payment CAPTURED.

history.title: History and Undo
history.body: Every change to the model leaves a version. Undo (Ctrl+Z outside text fields) goes back one step; from the History you compare a version with today and restore it.
history.example: A fix applied by mistake is undone with Ctrl+Z.

spec.hint: The domain document, always in sync with the model. For a PDF: Print → Save as PDF.
spec.openHint: The causes still open found by the edge case analysis (accepted ones excluded).

exp.title: Expectations
exp.subtitle: What the domain must allow: goals that must stay reachable and paths that must work. They are checked at every analysis: if a change breaks one, you see it right away.
exp.empty: No expectations yet. Add a goal (“it must be possible to reach Order DELIVERED”) or, from the simulator, save as a test a sequence of actions that must keep working.
exp.reach: It must be possible to reach
exp.reachedIn: Reachable with one action: | Reachable in {n} actions:
exp.unreachable: Unreachable: this combination is never reached from the initial state.
exp.noConditions: No conditions: add at least one.
exp.pathBlockedOk: It stops at step {n} (“{action}”), as expected.
exp.pathShouldBlock: It should be blocked, but it runs to the end.
exp.pathHint: Paths are created from the simulator: run the actions and press “Save as test” in the history.
exp.namePlaceholder: e.g. A paid order can be delivered
exp.saveTestHint: Save the sequence of actions as an expectation: it must keep working after every change
exp.saveTestDisabled: Only sequences of actions run from the initial state, without states set by hand or forced actions

ack.title: Or is it not a mistake?
ack.notePlaceholder: Why it is fine as is (optional)

current.accepted: Accepted: it no longer counts among open findings.
current.later: Postponed: it no longer counts among open findings.

ack.staleHint: It was accepted, but the part of the model involved has changed since then: it needs another look.

fix.title: Fix
fix.undoHint: The change is applied to the model right away; undo it with Undo (Ctrl+Z) or from the History.

preview.loading: Running the analysis on the changed model…

manual.default: There is no safe automatic fix for this case: open the entity and review the actions involved.
manual.deadlock: No action can run in this combination of states. Replay the path in the simulator: blocked actions show which guard stops them.
manual.dead_actions: The action can never run without conflicts: check its guards and, if it is cascade-only, that something triggers it.
manual.reachability: The state is never reached: no action leads to it, or the guards of those that do are never satisfied.
manual.relations: This is a hint about how relations are drawn: declare (or remove) them from the entity page.
manual.expectations: A domain expectation is no longer met. Open the Expectations: for a path, see where it gets stuck and why; for a goal, check the actions that should lead there.

state.livenessHint: Active: the entity exists and operates. Off: it exists but is disabled, and can be turned back on. Deleted: it no longer exists, with no way back. Compositions use it to decide what happens to the children.

home.title: Domains
home.subtitle: Each domain gathers entities, lifecycles, rules between entities and invariants. Start here to model your domain and hunt down edge cases.
home.confirmDelete: Permanently delete “{name}” and its whole model?
home.descriptionPlaceholder: Scope, actors, goal of the analysis…

model.compositionHint: {child} cannot exist without {parent}. The tool checks that creating it requires the parent, that the parent leaving the scene drags the children along, and that no reachable combination leaves a child alive without its parent.
model.instancesTitle: Children simulated per parent in the analysis
model.label: Label
model.instancesWarning: Applies to the analysis only (the simulator keeps one instance). It finds cases like "one child confirmed and the other deleted", but the combinations to explore grow fast: if the analysis is truncated, the results are partial.
model.livenessRule: When the parent is turned off, its children cannot stay active; when it is deleted, they must disappear.

states.title: State diagram
states.openErrors: {n} open error in the analysis | {n} open errors in the analysis
states.clean: No open errors in the analysis: the diagram describes a consistent model.

inv.title: Invariants
inv.subtitle: Combinations of states that must never exist at the same time. The simulator flags them live; the analysis searches for a path that reaches them.
inv.empty: No invariants yet. Example: “a SETTLED claim cannot have an assessment IN_PROGRESS”.
inv.derivedHint: Edit it from the relation, in the Overview.

sim.title: Simulator
sim.subtitle: Set the state of every entity (unusual combinations included) and see which actions remain available, which are blocked and which cause conflicts.
sim.noActions: No action can be executed from this combination of states.
sim.possibleDeadlock: Possible deadlock: some entities are not in a final state.
sim.forceTitle: Run ignoring guards and conflicts, to explore the edge case
sim.replayed: Path replayed: {n} step | Path replayed: {n} steps

analysis.title: Edge case analysis
analysis.subtitle: Explores every combination of states reachable from the initial state by applying guards and effects: finds violable invariants, cascading conflicts, deadlocks, dead states and dead actions.
analysis.loading: Exploring every reachable combination of states…
analysis.loadingHint: On large domains this may take a few tens of seconds. Results stay in memory until the model changes.
analysis.truncated: {partial} exploration: the combinations exceed the limit. The problems found are real, but others may be missing. Reduce the multiple instances for a complete analysis.
analysis.noIssues: No problems found with these filters.

view.showIssues: See the finding | See the {n} findings

analysis.shortestPath: Shortest path ({n} step) | Shortest path ({n} steps)
analysis.notReplayable: The path uses several instances of the same entity: the simulator has only one
analysis.matrixHint: Which pairs of states can coexist. The number tells in how many global states the pair appears.
analysis.cellReachable: reachable in {n} global state | reachable in {n} global states
analysis.showMissing: + {n} entity that does not exist | + {n} entities that do not exist
analysis.hideMissing: hide the ones that do not exist

entity.confirmDelete: Delete the entity “{name}” with its states, actions and related rules?
entity.statesHint: The entity's lifecycle. Final states end it.
entity.statesHintCreatable: Initial states are the ones reached by creation actions.
entity.statesHintInitial: One initial state, or several ways of coming into existence with creation actions.
entity.newStatePlaceholder: New state (e.g. IN_PROGRESS) and press Enter

birth.title: How it is created
birth.hint: Creation actions: every way the entity comes into existence, each with its own checks.

evolution.title: How it evolves
evolution.hint: State transitions with guards (preconditions on other entities) and cascading effects.

entity.noCreations: No creation actions: the entity starts from its initial state. Add one or more if it can come into existence in different ways.
entity.noActions: No actions: define how the entity changes state.
entity.cascadeOnlyHint: Not executed directly: it only happens as the effect of another action
entity.cascadeOnlyLong: Not executed directly: it only happens as the effect of another action (e.g. the credit note is issued only by recording the order return).
entity.matrixHint: Empty cells are unhandled combinations: check that this is intended.
entity.noDependents: No other entity looks at the state of {name}.
entity.guardsHint: Preconditions on the states of other entities (checked) or business rules (to verify by hand).
entity.eachHint: every {parent} (not deleted) must contain at least one {entity} in these states
entity.eachHintNot: no {parent} (not deleted) may contain a {entity} in these states
entity.noGuards: No guards: the action can always run from its source state.
entity.effectsHint: When the action happens, another entity must change state, run an action or be created. If it can't, it's a conflict.

effect.activeOnly: (skipped if already in a final state)
effect.createHint: the state is decided by the creation guards
effect.skipFinalHint: If the entity is already in a final state (e.g. CONFIRMED), the effect leaves it as is instead of reporting a conflict. Useful in 1-N relations: the effect only touches the instances still active and skips those already closed.

entity.statesHintGone: For each state, set whether the entity is active, off (recoverable) or deleted (final).

errors.title: One error on this entity | {n} errors on this entity
errors.hint: From the edge case analysis: cases where the entity, or an action involving it, gets stuck.

missing.title: One transition is missing | {n} transitions are missing
missing.hint: cascading effects of other entities that find no transition to run here

rel.title: Relations
rel.hint: How {name} is linked to the other entities. In compositions, what counts is the off and deleted states of each side.

map.title: Relation map
map.hint: {name} at the center, with its connected entities. Click an entity to open its page.
map.alone: {name} has no relations with other entities.
